newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs clear decision on satellite phones.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs clear decision on satellite phones.

text.p: The European Parliament approved on Thursday the Council common position on a planned system for regulating satellite phone systems in Europe.
Euro-MPs welcomed the plans, which will increase European coordination in selecting and licensing providers of satellite personal communications systems (S-PCS).
The draft decision, COM(95)529, reflects the European Commission's desire to organise the emerging market for dual-mode telephones, linked to both the terrestrial network and a satellite.
U.S.-led companies running S-PCS services are already seeking member states' authorisation to use their terrestrial equipment and frequencies.
However, the Telecommunications Council watered down a Commission's proposal to introduce a single EU-wide system for selecting and authorising satellite systems.

It asked the inter-governmental European Conference for Postal and Telecommunications Administrations to harmonise authorisation procedures, but left the final decisions in the hands of member states.

Rapporteur Karsten Friedrich Hoppenstedt, a German Christian Democrat, persuaded parliament to accept the Council's text with one amendment, on the grounds that it incorporated most of the changes demanded by Euro-MPs at first reading.
